def: The headquarters from which the JFACC plans, tasks, executes, and assesses air operations.
The commander who controls all joint and combined air operations for a JFC.
The overall commander of the joint force; sets the campaign objectives the JFACC supports.
A multinational, multi-service task force formed for a specific operation.
Joint Force Land Component Commander — commands all coalition land operations.
Joint Force Maritime Component Commander — commands all coalition maritime operations.
Joint Force Special Operations Component Commander — commands all coalition SOF operations.
The highest U.S. command authority. Held by a Combatant Commander. Cannot be transferred or delegated.
Authority to task and organize forces for specific missions. Can be delegated to a coalition commander.
Authority limited to local direction of movement and maneuver only. Does not include the right to assign missions.
Administrative authority — pay, personnel, training, maintenance. Always stays with the service or national force.
An operation involving two or more U.S. military departments together.
An operation involving U.S. forces plus partner or allied nation forces.
Forces from two or more US military departments operating together under one commander.
Forces from US and one or more partner or allied nations operating together.
The integrated system of agencies that manages air operations in a theater, from command down to execution.
A tactical-level team that requests and controls air support for a ground commander.
The qualified individual (typically within a TACP) authorized to control terminal weapons delivery.
The element that coordinates close air support requests between ground forces and the AOC.
A ground-based TACS agency that provides command and control of theater air defense and offensive air.
A JFACC-provided liaison element that coordinates air component requirements with other component commanders' staffs.
Wing-level command and control node that manages a wing's aircraft and coordinates with the AOC.
Airborne Warning and Control System — airborne radar and battle management focused on the AIR picture.
Joint Surveillance Target Attack Radar System — airborne radar focused on the GROUND picture and moving targets.
Tactical Air Coordinator (Airborne) — coordinates and manages multiple aircraft in a specific area.
Forward Air Controller (Airborne) — airborne qualified controller for terminal weapons delivery.
The executable order assigning specific sorties to specific missions for a given cycle. Produced by CPD.
The plan that pairs available aircraft with the target list and sequences strike packages. Produced by CPD; precedes the ATO.
Cycle-specific guidance issued by SRD that drives CPD's planning.
The long-range air campaign plan. Produced by SRD.
The airspace control plan for the cycle — coordinates airspace use and deconflicts users. Produced by CPD.
Cycle-specific instructions and ROE supplements attached to the ATO. Produced by CPD.
The prioritized list of targets approved for engagement in a given cycle. Developed and refined by the TET.
AOC division responsible for the JAOP, AOD, and campaign-level assessment.
AOC division responsible for translating the AOD into the MAAP, ATO, ACO, and SPINS.
AOC division responsible for executing the current ATO in real time. Operates 24/7.
AOC division responsible for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance support across the AOC.
AOC division responsible for Airlift, Air Refueling, and Aeromedical Evacuation.
Senior decision-maker on the COD floor. Holds personal authority for ROE and time-sensitive targeting decisions.
ISRD cell that fuses multi-source intelligence into finished products for the AOC.
COD team that manages data links and the Common Operating Picture.
ISRD position embedded on the COD floor; manages real-time ISR collection and re-tasking.
ISRD cell that formally tasks ISR assets and produces the RSTA Annex.
CPD team that nominates and vets targets for the JIPTL, conducts weaponeering, and performs collateral damage estimation.
Army liaison to the AOC. Coordinates ground force priorities and air support requirements.
Navy/Marine liaison to the AOC. Integrates carrier and amphibious air with the ATO.
SOF liaison to the AOC. Deconflicts SOF operations with conventional air.
The exercise of authority and direction by a commander over assigned forces — and the systems, procedures, and communications that make it possible.
A single shared display of the operational situation — friendly, enemy, and neutral — that all relevant nodes see in real time.
Operations to detect, intercept, and destroy enemy air and missile threats attempting to attack friendly forces or territory.
A commander-approved intelligence requirement critical to a planning or operational decision.
The intelligence-cycle stages after collection — preparing raw data, deriving intelligence, and pushing it to users.
Reconnaissance, Surveillance, and Target Acquisition Annex — the ISR tasking annex of the ATO.
Post-strike assessment of whether the desired effect was achieved.
Pre-strike analysis of expected collateral damage to civilians or non-combatant structures.
Directives that define when, where, and how force may be used by friendly forces.
The body of international law governing the conduct of hostilities; restricts how force may be applied (proportionality, distinction, military necessity, humanity).
A target that requires immediate engagement and is not on the planned ATO.
The process of engaging targets that arise during ATO execution and were not planned.
The coordinated acquisition, processing, and exploitation of accurate, relevant, and timely information to support commander decisions across all phases of an operation.
Intelligence derived from the interpretation of imagery (visible, infrared, radar).
Intelligence derived from intercepted communications (COMINT) and electronic emissions (ELINT).
Intelligence derived from non-communications electromagnetic emissions — radars, beacons, jammers, and other emitters.
Intelligence collected from human sources — interviews, debriefings, clandestine collection, and overt collection.
Intelligence derived from measurable signatures of objects and events (acoustic, seismic, radio-frequency, chemical, etc.) that identify or characterize them.
The integrated employment of information-related capabilities to influence, disrupt, corrupt, or usurp adversary decision-making while protecting friendly decision-making.
Air action against hostile targets in close proximity to friendly forces.
Operations to neutralize, destroy, or temporarily degrade enemy air defenses.
A system of systems combining radars, command and control, and interceptors.
A weapon or operation designed to destroy or degrade a satellite. Kinetic ASAT physically destroys; non-kinetic uses jamming, lasers, or cyber to disrupt without destruction.
Generic term for any satellite system that provides positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT). Includes GPS (US), Galileo (EU), GLONASS (Russia), BeiDou (China).
Air transport of patients in a permissive environment. AMD owns this through the AECT.
Recovery of personnel from hostile or denied territory. COD owns this through the PRCC.
In-flight transfer of fuel from a tanker aircraft to a receiver aircraft to extend range, endurance, or payload. One of AMD's three core mission sets.
AMD team that plans and coordinates airlift missions — moving cargo, personnel, and equipment by air.
AMD team that plans and coordinates tanker support and in-flight refueling for receiver aircraft.
AMD team that owns Aeromedical Evacuation planning and execution.
AMD team that monitors and tracks execution of all air mobility missions, providing situational awareness to the CMD.
The JFACC's primary advisor on all air mobility matters; the senior position in the AMD. Coordinates with AMC's TACC. (Not to be confused with the verb 'command'.)
The USAF major command (MAJCOM) that provides global airlift, air refueling, and aeromedical evacuation. Parent organization for the worldwide air mobility enterprise.
Air Mobility Command's 24/7 command and control center for global air mobility operations. The CMD coordinates theater mobility requirements with the TACC.
COD cell that owns Combat Search and Rescue coordination.
Specially organized, trained, and equipped forces that conduct missions requiring unique modes of employment, tactics, techniques, and procedures. Represented in the AOC by the SOLE.
An assessment writing convention: state the most important conclusion in the first sentence so the reader gets the answer immediately. Standard format for IC and military briefs.
A potential plan or option the adversary (or friendly force) might pursue. Analysts compare candidate COAs and identify the Most Likely (MLCOA) and Most Dangerous (MDCOA).
The adversary course of action most consistent with the convergence of current indicators. What the commander plans against.
The highest-impact adversary course of action that current indicators do not preclude. What the commander prepares branches against.

Policy issuances signed by the Director of National Intelligence that govern IC activities. ICD 203 sets the analytic standards (including the calibrated likelihood language) every finished IC product must follow.
A secured forward military position used to support tactical operations. Smaller and more austere than a main operating base; may be temporary.
Large multi-domain coercive state north of the Greater Caucasus. Primary adversary in this scenario. Currently occupying the Zabzimek Corridor inside Gorgas.
Western-leaning state south of the Caucasus ridge. NATO-aspirant. Primary coalition partner; the reason CJTF-CAU exists. Currently being invaded.
Coalition partner east of Gorgas; hosts the Coalition AOC at Atropian Air Base.

Constitution-based republic on the north shore of the Black Sea. Western-leaning majority population seeks NATO and EU membership; Donovia claims portions of eastern Pirtuni and backs separatist activity. Under sustained Donovian pressure but not Donovian-aligned.
Donovian-language separatist enclave inside Gorgas, currently seized by Donovian 58th Combined Arms Army. The principal objective for the coalition air campaign.
Host installation for the Coalition AOC, 220 km south of the Gorgas-Donovia border. The JFACC's primary command location.
